Integrated pest management, explained

Integrated pest management (IPM) keeps pests out by combining several methods, so chemicals are used only where they are needed:

  1. Inspection and monitoring: regular checks, monitoring stations and a log of sightings show where pests are and whether numbers are rising.
  2. Exclusion: sealing gaps around pipes and cables, fitting door sweeps and drain covers, and screening vents.
  3. Sanitation: fixing the conditions that attract pests, such as food spills, waste storage, standing water and clutter.
  4. Targeted treatment: gel baits, bait stations, traps and residual treatments placed where pests live, rather than blanket spraying.
  5. Review: trends from each visit are reviewed and the programme is adjusted.

What a commercial programme covers

  • Cockroaches in pantries, kitchens, washrooms and drains
  • Rodents at the perimeter, in stores, false ceilings and parking areas
  • Mosquitoes in compounds, terraces and construction areas, especially during the monsoon
  • Termites in wooden fittings, furniture and record rooms
  • Bed bugs in guest rooms, hostels and staff accommodation

Documentation for audits and inspections

For food businesses, healthcare facilities and companies with client or certification audits, the records matter as much as the treatment. You receive a treatment certificate after every visit, showing what was treated, with which products and when. Combined with the visit schedule, that gives you the evidence FSSAI inspectors, hospital accreditation assessors and client auditors ask for.

How often to treat

  • Commercial kitchens, restaurants and food production: usually monthly, with extra visits if activity is reported.
  • Offices and co-working spaces: usually quarterly, with monthly pantry checks in busy offices.
  • Warehouses: regular rodent monitoring, with the frequency set by the goods stored and the activity found.
  • Healthcare facilities: scheduled programmes planned around patient areas, with products chosen for sensitive environments.

Each site gets its own frequency after the first inspection.

FAQs

Pest Control Services: common questions

Can treatments be done outside working hours?

Yes. Commercial treatments are planned around your occupancy, which often means early mornings, evenings or weekends for offices and between services for kitchens.

What documentation do we receive?

A treatment certificate after every visit, showing the date, areas treated and products used. These are suitable for FSSAI, hospital accreditation and client audits.

Which products do you use?

WHO and CIB-approved products, chosen for the pest and the site. In sensitive areas such as kitchens and patient areas we rely on baits, traps and targeted treatments rather than broad spraying.

Do you cover multiple sites?

Yes. Multi-site programmes run on a common schedule and standard, with records for each location.
